- If sentiment is consistently negative or neutral in recent days, reduce forecast slope and avoid upward momentum; model tends to overreact to sentiment shifts.
- If forecast shows strong upward trend (e.g., >89.5) with recent sentiment >0.7, check for overshoot — true price often corrects downward within next 5–7 days.
- If true outcome shows sharp drop after a spike, model may have overestimated continuation — apply downward bias correction for 3–5 days post-spike.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.3) and forecast is rising, consider mean reversion — true price often pulls back toward prior 10–15 day average.
- For 30-day forecasts, if model is flat or slightly rising but true outcome shows volatility, reduce forecast slope by 10–15% to account for short-term noise.
- If sentiment history shows recent spikes (e.g., 0.9–1.0) followed by negative sentiment (e.g., -0.2 to 0.0), model may be overconfident — adjust forecast downward by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.
